subject: Re: DPA Q&A — EU processing, retention windows & deletion flow (redline proposal)
messages:
From: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@aurum.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@aurum.ai; Mira Patel <mira.patel@aurum.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: DPA questions: EU-only processing, retention & deletion process

Hi Grace,

Quick follow-up from our legal & infra teams after reviewing the draft DPA. Two main asks before we can move to signatures:

1) Residency: Can you confirm that all customer-generated content, logs, snapshots, and backups for our account can be processed and stored only in EU regions (we'd prefer europe-west1) with no cross-border transfers unless we explicitly authorize or local law requires it?

2) Retention & deletion: We need explicit windows and an accountable deletion flow. Specifically:
  - How long are request logs, inference logs (prompt + output), and model cache/kv entries retained?
  - What is the deletion timeline after a formal erase request or contract termination?
  - Are there any backup / snapshot retention exceptions (e.g., rolling backups, snapshots kept for recovery) and how are those erased?

Can you provide proposed redline language we can add to the DPA (we highlighted the relevant clauses) and a simple diagram or short table showing timelines we can share with auditors? We also need SOC 2 + latest pen-test report (or an ETA).

Thanks — can we have an initial response by tomorrow so procurement can schedule the signature call?

Lars
--
Lars Jensen
Head of Security, Aurum AI
lars.jensen@aurum.ai

Subject: Fwd: DPA questions: EU-only processing, retention & deletion process

Team — forwarding Aurum's questions. TL;DR: they want EU-only residency for all customer artifacts + concrete retention/deletion SLAs and backup wipe guarantees. Procurement wants a redline by tomorrow.

Key asks (from their legal):
- Confirm EU-only for customer content, logs, backups. They prefer europe-west1.
- Explicit retention windows for: request logs (who called API), inference logs (prompt/output), KV cache/short-term caches, backups/snapshots.
- A documented deletion flow with timelines for production data and backups after erase request or termination.
- SOC2 + pen-test — we usually provide SOC2 report and a summary of pentest findings; legal can request the full report under NDA.

Questions for you both:
- Karthik — can we commit to EU-only processing & storage for this account and propose fallbacks if we need cross-border for disaster recovery? What language can legal accept while keeping our ops flexible?
- Neha — please draft a short retention table (example rows: request logs, inference logs, KV cache, backups) with recommended windows (suggested: 30d request logs, 90d inference logs, 7d KV cache, 90–180d backups) and deletion certificate timeline (we usually do 30 days after erase request for final certificate; is that OK?)

I'll assemble your suggested redline and send back to Lars. Attachments: their flagged DPA (attached) — I'll include a first-pass redline once we agree.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: EU-only processing, retention & deletion process

Grace —

I've sketched a response and proposed language below. High level: we can commit to EU-only processing and storage at the account level if the customer requests and we pin their tenancy to EU regions. Operational notes:
- Backups and snapshots can be configured to remain in EU regions, but we retain the right to replicate metadata for orchestration/monitoring in our control plane which may be in another region. We should be explicit about metadata vs. content.
- Disaster recovery: if the customer requires multi-region DR that crosses borders, we need explicit authorization. Otherwise we keep DR copies in EU.
- Deletion: we can offer a 30-day finalization window for recovery before issuing a deletion certificate, with an exception for legal holds or regulatory retention. Backups: rolling backups may exist for up to 90 days; snapshot-level retention typically 90–180 days depending on the plan. We can accelerate retention if the customer elects an additional backup wipe SLA.

Proposed DPA language (suggested redline snippets):

"Proposed DPA language: 
1) Data Residency. Redwood will process and store Customer Data (as defined in Section X) exclusively within the European Union regional locations identified in the Order Form (\"EU Regions\"), unless Customer provides prior written authorization or applicable law requires otherwise. Metadata required for system health and billing (e.g., usage aggregations, telemetry identifiers) may be processed outside EU Regions but will not contain Customer content or PII.

2) Backups and Snapshots. Redwood will store backups and system snapshots in EU Regions. Rolling backups may be retained for a maximum of 90 days; full snapshots retained per the Service Plan up to 180 days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Upon Customer's written deletion request or termination, Redwood will: (a) delete active Customer Data within thirty (30) days; and (b) commence deletion of backups and snapshots within thirty (30) days and use commercially reasonable efforts to expunge recoverable copies within ninety (90) days. 

3) Deletion Certification. Following completion of deletion activities described above (subject to legal hold), Redwood will provide Customer with a written deletion certificate within thirty (30) days.

4) Cross-border Transfers. Any transfer of Customer Data outside EU Regions for operational reasons (including disaster recovery) will occur only with Customer's prior written consent or if compelled by law; Redwood will notify Customer in advance where reasonably practicable.

Notes:
- We should avoid promising 'irreversible immediate purging' of all backup media; for some storage layers immutable snapshots and vendor retention windows mean practical deletion is best-effort within the specified windows.
- If the customer insists on shorter backup windows or instant wipe guarantees, we can propose a paid add-on for expedited backup purge and on-prem snapshot destruction.

Neha: if you can turn the suggested retention numbers into a clean table (one-pager) I will author the redline doc and send to Aurum.

Karthik
Director, Product Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: EU-only processing, retention & deletion process

Hi Lars — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is our proposed redline (Redwood_DPA_redline_v2.docx) and a short retention summary table for auditors. Summary answers here so you can share immediately: 

- Residency: We can pin your tenancy to EU Regions (europe-west1) and ensure Customer Data and backups are stored and processed there. We will exclude cross-border transfers except with your prior written authorization or if compelled by law. We will, however, need limited metadata for control-plane operations; that metadata will not include Customer content or PII.

- Retention windows (recommended defaults — see attached PDF):
  • API request logs (routing + timestamp): 30 days
  • Inference logs (prompt + model output): 90 days
  • KV / ephemeral caches: 7 days (evicted automatically unless pinned)
  • Backups / snapshots: rolling backups kept up to 90 days; full snapshots up to 180 days depending on plan

- Deletion flow: Upon Customer's written erase request or contract termination: 
  1) Active data deletion initiated within 30 days.
  2) Backup deletion initiated within 30 days; commercially reasonable efforts to expunge recoverable copies within 90 days.
  3) Deletion certificate provided within 30 days of completion. Exceptions: legal hold or regulatory retention.

- SOC 2 + pentest: We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted pentest summary under NDA. I'll share the links via secure share once procurement confirms NDA.

Next steps: please review the redline doc attached and let us know any specific clauses you want tightened (e.g., shorten backup windows, require BYOK / HSM). If you prefer, we can book a 30-minute call Monday to walk the legal + infra team through it.

If Aurum wants BYOK as a condition, note that will require additional onboarding steps and a short lead time for KMS integration; we can add BYOK language to the DPA as an optional addendum.

Thanks —

Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
